name: RowanWeb Markdown for AI – .md Pages & llms.txt
author: Ryabinin Vitalii

sections.description:
AI assistants and RAG systems increasingly fetch site content directly, but they have to work through your theme’s HTML markup to do it — extra tokens, extra noise, and a real chance of misreading the actual content. This plugin gives them a clean alternative:

  • {permalink}.md — a markdown version of every public page, generated from the same rendered content your visitors see (post_content, blocks, shortcodes) and converted with a real HTML→Markdown parser, not a regex stripper. Headings, tables, links and images keep their structure.
  • /llms.txt — a dynamic index of public pages grouped by content type, with a short description for each. Every entry links both to the normal HTML page (so an AI citing your site points at a page a human can actually read) and to its .md version (for efficient re-fetching).
  • /llms-full.txt (optional, generated on demand) — a single file with the full markdown content of your most recent posts per content type (50 per type by default; set any number, or no limit, on the Settings tab), for tools that want more than the short index. Generated with one click on the Diagnostics tab; after content changes, an admin notice reminds you to regenerate it.
  • Deep custom-field support — if Advanced Custom Fields is active, the plugin automatically finds and renders every ACF field used on a page (any type, any nesting — repeaters, flexible content, groups) without any per-site configuration.
  • Privacy-safe by default — password-protected posts, drafts, and anything flagged noindex by your SEO plugin are never served as markdown. Per-post exclusion is also available from the editor sidebar.
  • Plays well with other SEO plugins — if Yoast SEO or Rank Math already generates its own llms.txt, this plugin automatically steps aside instead of racing for the same URL.
  • Pre-warmed, not lazy — markdown is rebuilt the moment you save a post, so the first crawler to arrive never waits on a cold cache. A bulk warm-up button covers existing content after activation.
  • robots.txt check — one click on the Diagnostics tab shows whether your robots.txt lets AI crawlers read the .md pages and llms files, which rule gets in the way and what to change. The plugin itself never edits robots.txt.
  • Bot activity log — see which AI crawlers actually visit your .md/llms.txt URLs, how often, and which exact pages, right in the Activity tab.
  • Multilingual-aware (Polylang) — on a multilingual site, llms.txt and llms-full.txt split into one section per language instead of mixing everything into a single list under one heading; custom-field labels are automatically translated to match each page’s own language.

A note on scope

This plugin is entirely about AI/LLM crawlers — it does not touch your normal SEO (Google, Bing, etc.), which your existing SEO plugin continues to handle exactly as before.

Pro version

RowanWeb Markdown for AI Pro is a separate, paid version. Everything described above works fully in this free plugin; Pro adds extra tools for busier sites:

  • Cloudflare cache purge — extends your existing Cloudflare plugin’s cache purge (or purges directly via your own API token if none is active) to also cover .md pages, llms.txt, and llms-full.txt whenever a post is saved.
  • Automatic llms-full.txt regeneration — the file rebuilds itself in the background shortly after relevant content is saved (bulk edits collapse into a single rebuild), so it never needs a manual click.
  • Weekly AI-crawler list updates — picks up newly launched AI crawlers from ai.robots.txt every week instead of waiting for the next plugin release. A plain download of a public file (no site data is sent), and it can be switched off.
  • CSV export — download the bot activity log as a CSV file for a spreadsheet or another analytics tool.
  • Rate limiting — throttle a recognized bot making too many .md/llms.txt requests per minute from one IP.
  • Suspicious-activity detection — flags requests probing for credentials or cloud metadata under a spoofed AI-bot User-Agent, listed separately from genuine crawler traffic.
  • Extra Activity reports — filter “Recent hits” by URL, plus “Hits per day” and “Top pages” (most-requested URLs with a per-bot breakdown).
  • Visitors from AI answers — people who followed a link to your site from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, Claude and similar services, by source and landing page, next to how often AI crawlers read the same page’s .md. Counted in the browser, so cached pages count too; no cookies and no personal data, only daily totals.
  • Live robots.txt monitoring — a daily check of robots.txt as crawlers get it, including rules a CDN such as Cloudflare adds, with an email to the site admin when it starts blocking AI crawlers.

External services

This plugin connects to the following third-party services. Nothing else is sent anywhere.

DeepL API (optional custom-field label translation)

If Advanced Custom Fields is active and you enter your own DeepL API key in Settings, the plugin uses the DeepL API (api-free.deepl.com or api.deepl.com, depending on your key) to translate custom-field labels (for example “Price” or “Specifications”) into your site’s language, for the section headings in .md and llms-full.txt output.

  • When: only after you add a DeepL API key — when you click “Translate field labels” on the Actions tab, or while a post is being saved / the cache is warmed / llms-full.txt is generated and a label hasn’t been translated yet. Never during a visitor’s or crawler’s request.
  • What is sent: the field label texts, the target language (and the source language, if you set one), and your API key. Post content is never sent. Translations are cached, so each label is sent only once.
  • Without an API key, nothing is ever sent to DeepL.
  • DeepL Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy.

Freemius (optional opt-in, licensing and updates of the Pro version)

The plugin includes the Freemius SDK, which handles the separate Pro version’s licensing and updates. In this free version, Freemius only shows an optional opt-in screen after activation.

  • When: only if you choose to opt in (or activate a Pro license).
  • What is sent: your site URL, WordPress and PHP versions, plugin version, site language, and the admin’s name and email address, plus plugin activation/deactivation/uninstall events. If you skip the opt-in, nothing is sent.
  • Freemius Terms of Service, Privacy Policy and details on what is collected.

Support

Questions, bug reports or feature requests: the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org, or https://rowan-web.ru/en/blog/rowanweb-markdown-for-ai-plugin-for-ai-crawlers/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the rowanweb-markdown-for-ai folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP via Plugins → Add New → Upload.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings → RowanWeb Markdown for AI and pick which content types should be included (posts, pages, and any custom post types you use).
  4. That’s it — {any public URL}.md and /llms.txt are live immediately.
sections.faq:
How do I check that the markdown version works?

Open any page on your site and add .md to the end of the address (remove a trailing slash first, if there is one) — you should get plain markdown text instead of the normal page.

Does it work with Advanced Custom Fields (ACF)?

Yes, with no setup. If ACF (free or Pro) is active, every field used on a page is added to its .md version and to llms-full.txt automatically, under its own heading. Supported field types include text, textarea, WYSIWYG, number, email, URL, link, select, checkbox, radio, true/false, image, gallery, post object, relationship, table, and nested group, repeater and flexible content fields. Field labels can optionally be translated into your site’s language with your own DeepL API key (see “External services”). If the automatic output misses something on a particular page, you can replace that page’s markdown by hand in the post editor.

Why doesn’t /llms.txt open, or it shows content I didn’t expect?

If your SEO plugin (Yoast SEO or Rank Math) already has its own llms.txt generation enabled, this plugin intentionally stays silent to avoid a conflict — the Diagnostics tab shows which plugin is currently serving it.

Where does the list of known AI crawlers come from?

It’s a snapshot of the community-maintained ai.robots.txt catalog (MIT License), bundled with the plugin and refreshed with each plugin release. Nothing is downloaded at runtime.

Does this affect my normal search engine SEO?

No. Search engines index your pages exactly as before. The extra files — .md pages, /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt — tell Google and Bing not to index them (an X-Robots-Tag: noindex addressed to googlebot and bingbot only), so they never compete with your pages in search results, while AI crawlers can still read them. The plugin does not change robots.txt.

Does the plugin change robots.txt?

No. Versions before 1.3.2 added a group of Allow rules for every known AI crawler; a crawler with its own group ignores the site’s User-agent: * rules, so that could switch off your other Disallow rules for those crawlers. Now robots.txt is left entirely to you, and the “robots.txt” check on the Diagnostics tab shows whether your rules let AI crawlers read the .md pages and llms files, and what to change if they don’t. The plugin also checks robots.txt daily and shows an admin notice if a rule closes the .md pages or llms files to AI crawlers by accident. Crawlers you closed completely on purpose don’t trigger it, and a site hidden from search engines (Settings → Reading) is never nagged.

Pro doesn’t update: “cURL error 35” or “Connection reset by peer”

The Pro update is downloaded from Amazon S3, where Freemius stores it; some hosting providers, mostly in Russia, block connections to it. The free version on WordPress.org is not affected. Download the current Pro zip from your Freemius account and upload it in Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin (WordPress offers to replace the current version), or ask your host to allow connections to *.amazonaws.com, or set a proxy with WP_PROXY_HOST and WP_PROXY_PORT in wp-config.php.

Does the plugin send any of my content anywhere?

No. Page content is only ever served in response to a normal HTTP request, exactly like any other page on your site. The plugin makes no outgoing connections on its own (the robots.txt check on the Diagnostics tab only loads your own site’s robots.txt, when you click it). The only exceptions are listed under “External services” below, and both are off until you turn them on: the DeepL translation of custom-field labels (only if you add your own DeepL API key) and the Freemius opt-in.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • Quieter notices. What needs your attention (llms-full.txt is older than your content, robots.txt blocks AI crawlers, Yoast SEO serves its own llms.txt) now shows as a count on the plugin’s menu item and in a “Needs attention” block at the top of its page, with a button that does the job there. Only real problems also appear on the Dashboard and Plugins screens, as one line with a dismiss button that keeps it hidden until something changes. No more notices on every admin screen.
  • Pro: “Visitors from AI answers” on the Activity tab — visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, Claude and others by source and landing page, with how often AI crawlers read each page’s .md. Counted in the browser (cached pages count too), without cookies or personal data.
  • Pro: the daily robots.txt check reads robots.txt as crawlers get it, so rules a CDN adds are seen too, and emails the site admin once when it starts blocking AI crawlers (can be switched off on the Pro tab).
  • Pro: no more “content changes have been synced” notice after each automatic llms-full.txt update; the Actions tab shows the file’s date and the next scheduled run.
  • A short “Thanks for updating” notice on the Plugins screen and the plugin’s page after an update with notable changes.
  • Runs on PHP 7.4 and newer (was 8.0).

1.3.4

  • The number of items per post type in llms-full.txt (50 by default, or no limit) and how long the bot activity log is kept (90 days by default, or forever) are now regular settings on the Settings tab, in every version. A retention period set earlier in Pro is carried over.
  • All database queries pass table names and values through $wpdb->prepare().
  • Deleting the plugin also removes the review-request state it kept.

1.3.3

  • robots.txt check: the groups older versions of this plugin added are only a warning, and only trigger the admin notice, when your User-agent: * group has Disallow rules they bypass; the warning now lists those rules. When User-agent: * disallows nothing, they are a tidy-up hint instead. The result comes first, and the note about a robots.txt file on the server shows only when there is something to fix there.
  • The robots.txt admin notice is hidden with a × in its corner, like other WordPress notices.
  • .md pages: a heading that is bold as a whole (## **Introduction**, when the editor put bold around the heading text) loses the redundant bold. Bold on part of a heading stays.
  • Diagnostics: published posts whose address is still WordPress’s placeholder auto-draft-N (typical after an import or a post created over the API) are listed with edit links, since AI crawlers see that address in llms.txt and the .md links.
  • A one-time request for a WordPress.org review on the plugin’s settings page, two weeks after installation and once AI crawlers have fetched at least 20 Markdown pages. Any click on it hides it for good.

1.3.2

  • robots.txt no longer gets a group of Allow rules for every known AI crawler. Such a group made those crawlers ignore the site’s own User-agent: * rules (your other Disallow lines stopped applying to them), and could override a crawler you had blocked yourself. Crawlers find the .md pages through the page’s <link> tag, the Link header and llms.txt, so nothing is lost.
  • New: robots.txt check on the Diagnostics tab. It reads your robots.txt the way crawlers get it and shows, for every known AI crawler, whether it may read your pages, their .md versions, llms.txt and llms-full.txt, which rule decides, and what to change. It also spots the groups older versions of this plugin added, Cloudflare’s managed robots.txt and a robots.txt file on the server. The same check also runs once a day in the background (without any network request) and shows an admin notice when robots.txt keeps AI crawlers away from the .md pages or llms files by accident; it can be hidden until something changes.
  • /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt now send the same search-engine-only X-Robots-Tag (googlebot:/bingbot: noindex) as .md pages, so Google and Bing no longer index them as plain-text pages; AI crawlers are unaffected.
  • The daily cleanup of the bot activity log is scheduled again if it goes missing. Switching from the free version to Pro could remove it, and the log then kept growing.
  • Pro: the settings export and import card is now a regular card on the Pro tab: Export and Import buttons, the backup’s status, and the details under “How it works”. Choosing a file asks for confirmation before importing.
  • The bundled Composer autoloader now has its own unique name, so it can never clash with another plugin’s (“Cannot redeclare class” when both are active).

1.3.1

  • Post types without a page of their own (for example, FAQ items shown only inside another page) are no longer offered or listed in llms.txt: their links led to “not found”.
  • No .md link is given for addresses without pretty permalinks (?p=123), where it could not work.
  • Pro: a more compact settings export and import card.

1.3.0

  • Elementor: pages built with Elementor now get their full content in .md and llms-full.txt in every context. Before, a .md rebuilt on save in wp-admin or in the background could come out empty or with only Elementor’s plain-text copy. Accordion and tab titles, counters’ final values and image boxes come out cleanly; duplicated tab titles and placeholder images are skipped.
  • Bricks: pages built with Bricks now get their content in .md and llms-full.txt. Bricks renders pages from its own template, not through the post content, so their .md used to be empty.
  • Cleaner markdown from page-builder markup: headings always use ## syntax, stray indentation no longer turns text into code blocks, and inline icons (SVG), forms, navigation (menus, breadcrumbs) and no-JS fallbacks are left out.
  • Lazy-loaded images now use their real address instead of the data: placeholder.
  • New: Meta Box, Pods and CMB2 fields are now added to .md and llms-full.txt, the same way ACF fields are — text, rich text, choices, images, files, related posts, terms, groups and repeatable fields. Their labels are included in “Translate labels”. CMB2 fields registered for wp-admin only are picked up on the front end too.
  • Select, radio and checkbox fields now show the option’s label (“Option B”) instead of its stored value (“b”), for ACF/Secure Custom Fields too.
  • Page builders’ internal post types (Elementor templates and floating buttons, Bricks, Beaver Builder, Oxygen and Divi templates) are no longer offered or included in llms.txt: they hold layout pieces, not content.
  • Pro: settings export and import. Download the plugin’s settings as a JSON file and import them on another site; API keys are left out unless you choose to include them, and importing a file without keys keeps the keys already set. Pro also adds a settings backup kept on the site itself (API keys included), restorable in one click and, if you choose, kept when the plugin is deleted.

1.2.1

  • Fixed: the .md version of the static “Posts page” (Settings → Reading), e.g. /blog.md, redirected to the HTML page instead of returning markdown, even though llms.txt lists it. The page now also gets its <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown"> and “View as Markdown” link.
  • Multilingual sites: language-prefixed /en/llms.txt and /en/llms-full.txt (e.g. from links in translated content) now 301-redirect to the root files instead of returning 404.
  • HTML pages now also advertise their .md version with a Link: <…>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown" HTTP header, for agents that only send a HEAD request.
  • New: content negotiation — a request for a page’s regular URL with Accept: text/markdown now gets the markdown version. Such responses are marked private and skip Cloudflare APO and page caches, so browsers never get markdown from a cache.
  • .md addresses with no post behind them (category and other archives, typos) now return a plain 404 instead of the HTML archive with status 200.
  • Multilingual sites (Polylang): llms.txt section headings now name their language (e.g. “Pages (English)”), and each .md front-matter lists links to its translations. Saving a post refreshes the cached .md of its translations.
  • Pro: all .md pages, llms.txt and llms-full.txt are purged from Cloudflare once after every plugin update, so posts you haven’t edited don’t keep serving an outdated cached copy. A “Purge all .md pages from Cloudflare” button on the Pro tab does the same on demand.

1.2.0

  • llms-full.txt is now stored in the uploads folder (wp-content/uploads/rowanweb-markdown-for-ai/) instead of the site root, and served at /llms-full.txt through WordPress. Requests to it now show up in the Activity tab.
  • The list of known AI crawlers is now bundled with the plugin; the free version no longer downloads it from GitHub.
  • Detection of a physical llms.txt left by another plugin now also works when WordPress is installed in a subdirectory.

1.1.2

  • Automatic background regeneration of llms-full.txt is now part of Pro. The free plugin generates it with the button on the Diagnostics tab and shows a reminder notice when content has changed since the last generation.
  • Pro: the “llms-full.txt may be out of date” notice no longer appears, since the file is regenerated automatically.

1.1.1

  • Renamed to “RowanWeb Markdown for AI” (new slug: rowanweb-markdown-for-ai).
  • Settings-page CSS and JavaScript are now proper enqueued files instead of inline blocks.
  • Stricter sanitization of request headers stored in the bot activity log.
  • The readme now documents every external service the plugin connects to.

1.0.5

  • Activating the plugin now redirects straight to its Settings page (skipped for bulk/network activation and WP-CLI, so it never hijacks an unrelated screen).
  • Added the missing Russian translation for the 1.0.4 “View as Markdown” badge toggle strings.

1.0.4

  • Added a Settings toggle to hide the floating “View as Markdown” badge for site visitors. AI/search crawlers are unaffected either way — they discover the .md version through the page’s <link rel="alternate"> tag and robots.txt, not through this badge.

1.0.3

  • Fixed the two scoped X-Robots-Tag headers on .md pages overwriting each other (PHP’s header() replaces a same-named header by default) — only the bingbot rule was ever actually being sent. Both now use $replace = false so Google and Bing each get their own rule.

1.0.2

  • The .md X-Robots-Tag header is now scoped to googlebot:/bingbot: instead of a bare noindex, so Google/Bing search still drop the page while AI crawlers that build their own retrieval index (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, and similar) see no restriction.

1.0.1

  • .md pages now send X-Robots-Tag: noindex, follow and a canonical Link header pointing at the original HTML page, so the markdown twin doesn’t end up duplicated in Google/Bing’s search index while staying fully fetchable by AI crawlers.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release: .md markdown pages, dynamic llms.txt, an optional full-content llms-full.txt dump, deep ACF field rendering, privacy controls, bot activity logging, multilingual (Polylang) support, and a Pro tier (Cloudflare cache purge, CSV export of the activity log, rate limiting, suspicious-activity detection, and deeper Activity-tab reporting).

short_description: Markdown for AI crawlers: a clean .md version of every page (ACF fields included), a dynamic llms.txt, and a log of which AI bots read them.

screenshots.caption: Diagnostics tab: llms.txt status, which SEO plugin (if any) is already handling it, and system info.
Activity tab: bot hit stats and the most recent requests, filterable by bot.
Actions tab: label translation, cache warm-up, and llms-full.txt generation.
Settings tab: choosing which content types are included and other one-time setup.
